verdict.rationale: Spline's own docs describe a no-code states/events/actions interactivity model, plus webhooks and a Real-time API that automatically trigger actions and responses on events, so the core event→action capability is first-party. The evidence is mostly one-line claims, and the automation is scene-level interactivity rather than broad workflow automation. Missing for 10: documentation of the supported event types and conditional rule logic, the depth and limits of the action set, and independent or hands-on corroboration that event-triggered rules work as described.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Most interactivity in Spline needs no code at all. It's built from **states, events and actions**
By using webhooks, your Spline project can automatically trigger actions, update variables, and react to data sent from external sources
The Real-time API feature in Spline allows you to integrate external services, retrieve or send data, and automate responses based on events.
It's possible to transition between scenes with the Events system by using a Scene Transition action.
